questions.q: Why does this lesson deliberately avoid quoting a specific quant salary figure?
options: Because quant salaries are a secret that cannot legally be discussed
Because compensation figures go stale quickly and vary enormously by firm type, strategy, and city, so an invented or outdated number would do more harm than good
Because quant roles are never compensated with a base salary
Because only recruiters are allowed to discuss compensation
questions.explain: Rather than quoting a number that could be wrong or outdated, the lesson teaches the research process for building your own evidence-based range for your specific situation.

questions.q: How does compensation structure typically differ between a prop trading firm and a bank quant desk (sell-side)?
options: They are always identical in structure
Prop trading firms often use a lower base with bonus/profit-share heavily tied to individual or desk trading performance; bank desks typically tie bonus more to overall bank/division performance
Bank quant desks never pay any bonus at all
Prop trading firms only pay in equity, never cash
questions.explain: Prop shops tend to link pay more directly to individual/desk PnL, producing more variance, while bank quant desks tie bonuses more to broader division or firm performance.

questions.q: Why can two offers with the same headline base salary represent very different real outcomes?
options: Base salary is the only thing that ever matters in a compensation package
A profit-share-heavy structure can pay far more in a good year and far less in a bad year than a steadier, more bank-like bonus structure, even with the same base
Equity compensation is identical at every firm by law
There is no real difference once the base salary matches
questions.explain: Understanding whether an offer's bonus/profit-share component is PnL-linked or more steady and discretionary matters as much as the base number, since it drives very different variance in total pay.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend evaluating beyond the compensation number when choosing between competing offers?
options: Nothing else matters besides total compensation
Strategy and risk-culture fit, mentorship and learning curve, stability of the pay structure, and what the role actually does day to day
Only the firm's office location
Only the length of the interview process it took to get the offer
questions.explain: The lesson recommends weighing risk culture, mentorship, pay-structure stability, and the actual day-to-day nature of the role alongside the compensation figure itself.

questions.q: What is the recommended approach to building a researched compensation range before a number comes up in conversation?
options: Rely on a single number remembered from an online forum
Combine at least two independent sources (aggregated salary sites, live postings, your own network) specific to the firm type and city being evaluated
Ask only the hiring manager and accept whatever figure they offer first
Average together numbers from completely different firm types and cities
questions.explain: A reliable range comes from at least two independent sources, specific to the actual firm type and city in question — averaging unrelated firm types or cities produces a meaningless middle figure.
